subject: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

Hi Naomi,

We’re prepping the public-facing benchmark report + interactive table launch next week. Before we cut the final docs-site PR and flip the endpoint public, could you do a security review specifically on the “public artifacts” we plan to publish?

Artifacts (planned public):
- Versioned results JSON/CSV (for the interactive table)
- Methodology summary page
- (Potentially) a small “reproducibility pack” with run manifests + config templates (no raw logs)

We’ve attached a sample zip that matches what would be served publicly.

Key question: do any of the artifacts reveal sensitive operational details (fleet, capacity, internal hostnames, request IDs, etc.) that we should redact or avoid publishing entirely?

Time sensitivity: would be ideal to get guidance today so we can implement in the pipeline + docs copy by tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Soojin
—
Soojin Lee
Director of Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

Attachment: public-artifacts-sample.zip
Attachment: benchmark_results_schema_v1.md
Attachment: redaction-checklist_v0.3.docx


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

Thanks — I pulled and reviewed the zip.

High-level: the results JSON/CSV is directionally fine, but the “run-manifest.json” contents (as currently exported) include a few fields we should not publish as-is.

Items to redact or remove before public release:

1) Internal identifiers / infrastructure fingerprints
- cluster / fleet identifiers (e.g., "fleet": "gpu-fleet-eu-west-3a" / similar)
- node pool names and k8s namespaces
- internal hostnames and service names
- any IPs (public or private) and VPC identifiers

2) Capacity + procurement signals
- exact instance type strings and GPU SKU detail (e.g., “H100-80GB SXM”, “a3-megagpu-8g”, etc.)
  - Recommend: publish a normalized “hardware_class” value (e.g., "H100-class", "L40S-class") and keep exact types internal.
- any fields that indicate reserved capacity or queue depth / scheduler detail

3) Potentially sensitive operational timing
- run start timestamps at high precision + region + hardware can be used to correlate with internal status/incident timelines
  - If we need timestamps at all: downsample to date only (YYYY-MM-DD) or publish the “benchmark window” as text, not per-run timestamps.

4) Traceability fields
- request_id / trace_id / span_id equivalents
  - Even if they look random, they often map to internal logs or are used across systems.

5) Cost breakdown fields
- I did not see direct $/hour GPU pricing, but the manifest includes a “cost_inputs” section with enough granularity to back into internal assumptions if paired with throughput.
  - Recommend: publish derived “$/1M tokens” and “latency/$” only; keep intermediate cost inputs internal.

What I’d keep:
- model name + version label (public)
- region label (cloud region is OK)
- high-level config knobs (concurrency, context length, streaming on/off) as long as they are phrased generically

Actionable recommendation:
- Strip the run-manifest to a “public manifest” schema with an explicit allowlist of fields.
- Have the pipeline fail closed: if any non-allowlisted keys appear, block the export job.

If Engineering already has a redaction PR, happy to comment on the exact fields they should allowlist.

Naomi
—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 10:26 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

Naomi — super helpful.

Quick clarifying Q: for the interactive page, we currently show:
- provider region (e.g., us-east / eu-west)
- model
- context length bucket
- p50/p95 + throughput + $/1M tokens + latency/$

No run timestamps shown on the page, but the JSON includes per-run timestamps for debugging.

Is it sufficient if we remove timestamps from the public JSON entirely and keep them only in the internal dataset (used for validation + audit)?

Ben


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

Yes — that’s the cleanest approach.

Recommendation:
- Public JSON/CSV: no per-run timestamps, no per-run IDs.
- Internal dataset (restricted): keep timestamps + run_id + manifest hash for auditability.

One nuance: if we anticipate external critique and want to show “repeatability,” publish aggregated stability metrics (e.g., N runs, variance bands) rather than raw run-by-run artifacts.

Also: avoid including any “runner_version” that encodes internal build metadata (commit SHA is OK if it’s already public, but not internal image registry paths).

Naomi


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 12:14 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

Naomi — great.

Two things we’re debating internally:

A) Publishing a small “repro pack”
- Proposed: methodology + prompt set description + CLI example + config template
- Not proposed: raw logs or raw manifests

B) “Hardware transparency” language
- Sales wants to say “H100 results” explicitly.

Given your notes, can we:
- Mention “H100-class GPUs” in the PDF/blog, without listing exact SKU/instance type?
- Include CLI examples that show parameters (model, region, concurrency) but redact internal endpoints + image names?

I want to avoid a last-minute legal/security rewrite.

Soojin


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 1:22 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

A) Repro pack: yes, with guardrails.
- OK to publish: CLI examples + config template + schema + methodology narrative.
- Ensure examples do NOT include:
  - internal domains (anything *.corp / internal DNS)
  - internal container registry references
  - flags that expose fleet topology (pool/cluster names)
  - any auth/token examples beyond placeholders
- Make sure anything that looks like a real token is synthetically invalid (e.g., "REDACTED"), not just truncated.

B) Hardware language: “H100-class” is acceptable.
- Avoid exact instance type strings.
- Avoid calling out specific cloud provider instance families if that maps 1:1 to capacity planning.
- If you must list vendor names (e.g., NVIDIA), do it at the “GPU family” level.

Additional redaction items I noticed in the sample export:
- The manifest contains “cdn_pop” / edge identifiers. Remove.
- There’s a “fallback_region_attempts” list. Remove (exposes routing behavior).
- Remove “queue_time_ms” and “scheduler_wait_ms” if present; those are operationally sensitive.

If you want, send me the final intended public schema and I’ll do a fast pass with an explicit allowlist.

Naomi


---

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: public benchmark artifacts (redaction + exposure risks)

Naomi — thanks for turning this around quickly.

Soojin/Ben: please implement Naomi’s allowlist approach and remove per-run timestamps/IDs from anything public. Let’s also align the “H100-class” phrasing and avoid instance family callouts.

Naomi: once we have the final public schema, we’ll send it your way for a last look before we publish.

Camila
—
Camila Reyes
VP Marketing
Redwood Inference
